We need to propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: steps are (in forward direction):
1. Carboxylic acid to amide (coupling) -> So retrosynthesis: break amide to give carboxylic acid and amine.
2. Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> alpha,beta-unsaturated carboxylic acid. So retrosynthesis: break the C=C and carboxylic acid to give aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid? Actually forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> unsaturated acid. So reverse: unsaturated acid -> aldehyde + malonic acid (or malonate). So we need to identify the fragment: the unsaturated acid is /C=C/C(=O)N... Actually the unsaturated acid part is /C=C/C(=O)N... Wait the target has /C=C/C(=O)N... The unsaturated acid is the alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl attached to an anilide. The Doebner modification would produce the unsaturated acid from an aldehyde (aryl aldehyde) and malonic acid, then decarboxylation yields the unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid). So retrosynthesis: the unsaturated acid fragment (cinnamic acid derivative) can be derived from corresponding aldehyde (aryl aldehyde) and malonic acid. So step 2: break the C=C and the carboxyl to give aldehyde (aryl aldehyde) and malonic acid.

3. Sulfonamide formation: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide. So retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl halide) and amine.

Thus overall route:
Target -> (1) break amide: gives unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid derivative) + aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). Actually the amide is C(=O)N attached to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So retrosynthesis step 1: target -> unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid attached to phenyl sulfonyl) + aniline (c3ccccc3N). The unsaturated acid still has sulfonamide attached to phenyl-sulfonyl group.

Step 2: break unsaturated acid into aldehyde (aryl aldehyde) + malonic acid. The aldehyde would be the aryl ring attached to sulfonyl? Actually the unsaturated acid is attached to the sulfonyl phenyl ring via the double bond: /C=C/C(=O)N... The double bond is conjugated to the phenyl-sulfonyl ring? The structure: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the unsaturated acid is attached to the phenyl ring (the sulfonyl phenyl). So the aldehyde precursor would be the same phenyl ring with an aldehyde substituent: c2ccc(CHO)cc2 (para to sulfonyl?). Actually the double bond attaches at para position of that phenyl ring. So aldehyde is p-formyl phenyl sulfonyl? Wait the sulfonyl is attached to that phenyl ring via S(=O)2 attached to that phenyl. The unsaturated acid attaches at para position relative to sulfonyl? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the phenyl ring has substituent /C=C/... at position 1 (maybe para to sulfonyl). So aldehyde would be c2ccc(C=O)cc2 (para aldehyde). So step 2: break unsaturated acid to give p-formyl phenyl sulfonyl (i.e., p-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl remains attached to the phenyl ring; the aldehyde is on that phenyl ring. So we need the aldehyde with sulfonyl group attached? The sulfonyl is attached to the phenyl ring via S(=O)2 attached to the phenyl (the same phenyl). So the aldehyde precursor would be the same phenyl-sulfonyl group with aldehyde substituent: p-formyl phenyl sulfonyl (maybe as sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl is part of the sulfonamide later). At this stage, we have not yet broken sulfonamide; the sulfonamide is still present (the sulfonyl attached to the other phenyl ring via S-N). Wait the sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O)c2... So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl (toluene ring) and the sulfonyl attached to second phenyl (the one with unsaturated acid). So after step 1, we have the sulfonamide still intact (the N-SO2-aryl). So step 2 deals with the aryl sulfonyl phenyl bearing the unsaturated acid side chain. The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl (toluene). So step 2 does not affect sulfonamide.

Thus step 2: unsaturated acid (aryl-sulfonyl phenyl with side chain) -> aldehyde (aryl-sulfonyl phenyl with CHO) + malonic acid.

Step 3: break sulfonamide: gives sulfonyl chloride (aryl-sulfonyl chloride) and aniline (the toluene ring with amine). Actually the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the toluene ring (with methyl). So breaking gives p-toluidine (with methyl) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (the other phenyl). So final precursors: p-toluidine (C c1ccc(N)cc1) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (Cl-SO2-aryl with aldehyde). Also need malonic acid and aniline (c3ccccc3N) as separate? Wait the amide step gave aniline (c3ccccc3N) as amine partner. So final set of precursors: p-toluidine, aryl sulfonyl chloride (with aldehyde), malonic acid, aniline (or maybe the aniline is part of amide formation with the unsaturated acid; after step 1 we have unsaturated acid + aniline). So total precursors: p-toluidine, aryl sulfonyl chloride (with aldehyde), malonic acid, aniline. That's 4 building blocks, but route has 3 reactions, each reaction may involve two reactants.

We need to produce a JSON route with 3 reaction nodes.

We need template IDs for each step. We can search for templates matching each transformation.

Step 1: amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine -> amide). Search for functional_groups_broken: amide, formed: aliphatic carboxylic acid, primary amines? Actually forward: acid + amine -> amide, breaking O-H and N-H, forming C-N. In retrosynthesis, we break amide to give acid and amine. So we need a template that does that. Let's search with broken: amide, formed: aliphatic carboxylic acid, primary amines. Already attempted and got empty. Maybe need to specify functional_groups_broken: ["amide"] and formed: ["aliphatic carboxylic acid", "primary amines"] but got empty. Could be that template not present. Could use generic amide hydrolysis template? Let's search for functional_groups_broken: ["amide"] only.
